dedupe_keys.name: digital twin simulation of predictive freight routing on inland waterways under water level uncertainty

description: This preprint, submitted to IEEE Digital Twin 2026, studies whether a digital twin can improve freight routing on inland waterway networks when water levels are uncertain. The authors note that climate-driven volatility in water levels raises operating costs and emissions when cargo must move to costlier modes such as road transport, and that existing practice relies on reactive countermeasures. Six interviews with experts in inland shipping identified three common contingency scenarios and the operational responses to them. These scenarios were built into a time-sliced simulation environment in which predictive decisions enabled by the digital twin were compared with reactive ones. Predictive decisions substantially reduced operating costs and modal shifts at prediction accuracies between 70% and 100%, even under extreme conditions, and cut fuel-related costs by 28.3% on average by reducing the distance ships travel. The results were reviewed with domain experts. Access: arXiv preprint of 11 June 2026, 6 pages. Licence and cost: free to read. Caveats: a short conference preprint, not peer reviewed, with a stylised network and no released code. It illustrates digital twin, optimisation and climate adaptation uses for waterway logistics. It relates to the Rhine 2018 low water case study and the BfG Rhine water level forecasts in the catalogue.
